Industrio Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Industrio Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Director of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Industrio Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; and Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Industrio Corp.'s performance for the third quarter of 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering robust results across our core segments while advancing key strategic priorities in a dynamic industrial landscape. Notably, our aftermarket parts and services business continued its impressive trajectory, providing high-margin, recurring revenue that now forms a larger portion of our overall mix. We've also seen strong operating margin expansion in key areas like industrial machinery and aerospace, driven by pricing discipline, volume leverage, and operational enhancements from our lean initiatives. Our dividend remains a key pillar of shareholder returns, with another increase underscoring our confidence in free cash flow generation. And looking forward, end-market demand signals point to stabilization in the near term evolving into stronger growth over the medium term, fueled by automation, electrification, and reshoring trends.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives— including IoT-enabled platforms, nearshoring expansions, and targeted M&A—are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth amid the ongoing transformation of manufacturing.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Rivera (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. Turning to our financial performance, Industrio Corp. reported $2.85 billion in revenue for the third quarter, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 36.2%, driven by favorable product mix, pricing actions, and efficiencies in our supply chain. Operating expenses were $685 million, resulting in an operating income of $392 million. Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.85 per diluted share.

We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet, with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and net debt to EBITDA at a healthy 1.4 times. We are committed to investing in our business to drive future growth and shareholder value.

Before we open the floor to questions, let me provide some additional color on several key areas that highlight the strength and resilience of our results. First, on our dividend policy and yield, which remains a cornerstone of our capital allocation strategy in this cyclical industry. As you know, Industrio has a proud history of returning value to shareholders through a disciplined, sustainable approach. We target a payout ratio of 45% to 55% of adjusted diluted EPS, balanced against our free cash flow conversion, which averaged 95% over the past 12 months. This framework has enabled us to navigate volatility in industrial equipment demand, such as automotive OEM retooling for electric vehicles, aerospace aftermarket recovery following Boeing 737 MAX challenges, and construction equipment upcycles linked to infrastructure investments.

For the third quarter, we declared a quarterly dividend of $0.48 per share, payable on November 15th to shareholders of record as of October 25th. That's a 6% increase year-over-year and marks our 28th consecutive quarterly hike. Annualized, this equates to $1.92 per share, delivering a forward yield of 2.7% at yesterday's close of $71.11—positioning us competitively in the mid-cap industrials space. For context, that's ahead of Caterpillar's 1.8% yield and in line with Parker Hannifin's profile but with a higher growth trajectory; our 10-year dividend CAGR stands at 9.2%, outpacing the S&P 500 Industrials index by 350 basis points.

Our payout ratio for the trailing 12 months came in at 48.2% of adjusted EPS of $3.98, well within our band and supported by robust free cash flow of $425 million in Q3 alone—up 12% year-over-year despite lapping last year's supply chain tailwinds from the resin shortage in hydraulic seals. We generated $1.72 billion in operating cash flow year-to-date, converting 112% to free cash flow after $280 million in capex, primarily directed toward our new 150,000 square foot automation robotics facility in Monterrey, Mexico. This nearshoring initiative is yielding early wins, with Q3 bookings from North American auto tier-1 suppliers up 22% as they diversify away from China amid USMCA tariffs.

Regionally, our dividend sustainability is underpinned by diversified end-market exposure. North America contributed 52% of Q3 revenue, driven by strong aftermarket parts for legacy machine tools amid a 15% year-over-year rise in US industrial production excluding autos. APAC, at 28% of the mix, saw 18% organic growth from demand for our next-generation fiber-laser CNC machines in China's EV battery gigafactory buildout, with suppliers like CATL and BYD ramping capex. EMEA remains challenged at 15% of revenue, with a 4% decline due to lingering energy costs impacting German machinery capex, but our 65% localization rate there via our Dortmund hydraulic plant has preserved margins at 24.2%.

Strategically, we're focused on balancing shareholder returns with reinvestment in secular tailwinds reshaping industrial equipment. Industry 4.0 adoption is accelerating—our IoT-enabled SmartForge platform, now on 40% of new hydraulic presses, has boosted service attach rates to 32% of revenue, up from 28% last year, providing high-margin, recurring cash flows that de-risk our dividend. We're also prioritizing electrification: Q3 R&D spend of $65 million advanced our 48V electro-hydraulic actuators, targeting a $4.5 billion total addressable market in off-highway equipment by 2028 according to McKinsey estimates. This positions us to capture share from incumbents like Eaton in the green transition, while our balance sheet gives us dry powder for bolt-ons, like the recent $150 million tuck-in acquisition of a Polish robotic welding arm manufacturer.

Looking ahead, we reaffirm our commitment to dividend growth of 7-10% annually through the cycle, contingent on free cash flow growth from our $2.8-3.0 billion 2025 guidance. We've stress-tested this against downturn scenarios, including a 15% drop in global capex similar to 2020, and remain confident in coverage ratios above 1.8 times. In a yield-hungry environment with 10-year Treasuries at 4.2%, our 2.7% yield plus 9% EPS growth offers a compelling total return profile—our five-year total shareholder return of 180% beats 85% of industrial peers.

Shifting to one of our most resilient growth engines: aftermarket parts and services. This segment delivered another quarter of double-digit expansion and continues to grow its share within our total revenue mix, underscoring our strategic shift toward servitization in the industrial equipment space. In Q3, aftermarket parts and services revenue reached $970 million, up 16% year-over-year and 4% sequentially from Q2. This extends our streak to 12 straight quarters of at least 15% year-over-year growth, significantly outpacing new equipment sales. As a percentage of our total Q3 revenue of $2.85 billion, aftermarket now represents 34%, an all-time high and up 400 basis points from last year. This outperforms peers like Caterpillar, where aftermarket typically runs 30-32% of parts and services revenue, or Ingersoll Rand at around 28%. Our margin profile here is exceptional, with segment-adjusted EBITDA margins at 68%—nearly triple the 23% in new equipment—thanks to 65% plus gross margins on parts, low variable costs in services, and ongoing scale efficiencies.

Breaking it down, parts revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $610 million, supported by higher utilization rates across our installed base of over 1.2 million units worldwide. This includes hydraulic pumps, conveyor bearings, and precision gearboxes for our material handling and automation lines—average selling prices rose 6% due to greater adoption of premium wear parts as supply chains stabilize. Services revenue was the standout at $360 million, up 20% year-over-year, driven by a surge in predictive maintenance contracts and uptime guarantees. Our Dynalink IoT platform, now deployed on 45% of our active fleet—up from 32% a year ago—was pivotal. Leveraging edge analytics and machine learning for anomaly detection, we've cut unplanned downtime by 22% for customers, lifting mean time between failures from 2,800 to 3,500 hours on average for our CNC machining centers and automated guided vehicle fleets. This builds on successes akin to Rockwell Automation's FactoryTalk or Honeywell's Forge, but our proprietary sensor fusion technology provides a 15-20% edge in predictive accuracy.

Regionally, North America, at 48% of aftermarket revenue, grew 18% year-over-year to $465 million, fueled by reshoring and capex recovery in semiconductors and EVs. Key OEM partners in battery gigafactories are emphasizing uptime amid labor constraints, driving 25% uptake in our subscription-based Uptime Assurance packages—now covering over 60,000 units with service level agreements guaranteeing 98.5% availability. APAC grew 19% to $310 million, or 32% of the segment, on infrastructure surges in India and Southeast Asia; partnerships with Komatsu and SANY for hybrid excavator fleets unlocked $50 million in new service contracts tied to Belt and Road expansions. EMEA, representing 15% or $145 million, advanced 9% despite energy volatility and destocking, but we're building share via localized remanufacturing in Germany, eyeing 12-15% growth in the second half as wind farm operations and maintenance accelerates.

This momentum stems from targeted investments, including $120 million year-to-date in digital twins and augmented reality-assisted field service through our RemoteExpert app, which has reduced technician dispatch times by 35% and enabled 24/7 remote diagnostics for 70% of high-value assets like power generation turbines. We're also pursuing M&A in the aftermarket space, highlighted by the $250 million acquisition of Apex Reman, adding hydraulic cylinder rebuild expertise and instantly lifting recurring revenue by 8%. We anticipate aftermarket reaching 38% of total revenue by fiscal 2025, bolstered by a 1.5 times aging fleet multiplier—our installed base now averages 7.2 years old, ideal for upgrades—and disciplined pricing amid easing steel costs. Full-year growth is pegged at 15-17%, with Q4 guidance at $990-1.01 billion. Aftermarket truly serves as our economic moat, generating sticky, high-margin cash flows to fund R&D in electrification and autonomy.

Next, let's unpack our operating margin performance by segment, which stood out this quarter against a choppy macro backdrop. Overall, we achieved a consolidated operating margin of 13.8%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points from Q2. This reflects our disciplined pricing, supply chain resilience, and returns from our $250 million Enterprise Lean Sigma program, featuring digital twins for CNC lines and AI-driven inventory optimization across 45 global plants.

Our largest segment, Industrial Machinery at 42% of Q3 revenue or $1.2 billion—up 8% year-over-year—saw margins expand to 15.4%, a 190 basis point gain that outruns Caterpillar and Illinois Tool Works. Double-digit volume growth in automation equipment, including 25% uptake of our modular robotic palletizers for North American e-commerce fulfillment centers like Amazon and FedEx sites, was key. Pricing rose 4.2% despite 6% higher steel costs from Red Sea issues. APAC margins reached 17% on reshoring in China's semiconductor fabs, while EMEA was 13% softer on German auto OEM demand. Our Machinery 4.0 platform, with IoT for predictive maintenance, trimmed COGS by 2% via 15% fewer downtimes.

Aerospace & Defense, 28% of revenue at $785 million and up 12% year-over-year on Boeing 737 MAX and Airbus A320neo ramps, hit 18.2% margins—a 320 basis point surge, leading peers like Honeywell and RTX. Supply chain normalization recaptured 150 basis points from earlier titanium delays. Aerostructure composites for GE Aviation's LEAP engines drove 30% of segment EBIT, with aftermarket MRO adding 100 basis points. North America led at 20% margins on 80% of growth; Europe was 16% on Pratt & Whitney inspections. A $100 million push into additive manufacturing for titanium brackets eyes F-35 contracts and 20% plus margins by fiscal 2025.

Energy Equipment, 18% of revenue at $510 million and up 5% year-over-year, faced Brent crude at $82 per barrel below our $90 breakeven for upstream kits, compressing margins to 10.1% or down 50 basis points, in line with SLB and Halliburton. Renewables grew 22%, with wind turbine gearboxes for Vestas and Siemens Gamesa at 14% margins via our Odisha, India facility cutting logistics 18%. LatAm was 12% on Petrobras FPSO; Middle East 9% on OPEC+ cuts. We're allocating 40% of fiscal 2024 capex to hydrogen electrolyzer components with Plug Power, aiming for mid-teens margins by 2026 on IRA momentum.

Automotive Systems, 12% at $340 million and flat year-over-year amid EV shifts, posted 8.5% margins—up 60 basis points sequentially but down 90 year-over-year, tracking Magna and BorgWarner. Chip shortages delayed ADAS sensors and shifted 10% mix to lower-margin battery jigs for GM Ultium; pricing added 150 basis points offset half by Monterrey labor costs. APAC improved to 10% on Toyota hybrids; North America 7% on strikes. Our EV Forge robotic welding for gigacastings like Tesla's 4680 cells boosted throughput 20%, set to add 200 basis points in Q4.

Overall, these segments highlight resilience: Industrial and Aerospace as engines, Energy transitioning to renewables, Automotive navigating EVs. Free cash flow conversion at 95% supported $400 million buybacks and a 12% dividend increase.

Finally, as we wrap results, our outlook for end-market growth across manufacturing and industrial equipment verticals. Forward-looking statements are subject to 10-K risks like supply chains, tariffs, and macro headwinds, but visibility is solid with a $4.2 billion backlog, up 12% year-over-year or over 10 months of revenue.

Near-term through calendar 2025: 4-6% overall end-market growth, up from flat-to-down 1-2% this year, as destocking eases and plant utilization hits 78% globally per our surveys, from 72% last year.

By end market: Semiconductor and electronics (25% mix) at 10-12% on AI chip demand from NVIDIA, TSMC HBM ramps, and CHIPS Act grants for Intel, Samsung fabs—pulling our CNC and wafer tools like Applied Materials' backlog. Automotive (20%) 3-5% on EV retooling for Ford, GM platforms and gigafactories offsetting ICE. Aerospace & Defense (18%) 5-7% on Boeing, Airbus aiming 800+ aircraft yearly; 18-month bookings for turbine tools echo GE. Construction & mining (15%) 2-4% pressured by rates but aided by $550 billion IIJA. General industrial & renewables (22%) flat to 3%, with solar trackers up 15% offsetting wind deferrals.

Regionally: North America (45%) 6-8% on IRA, CHIPS reshoring—US orders up 18% quarter-over-quarter. Europe (25%) 1-3% on energy, German autos; pivoting East for batteries. APAC (25%) 4-6%, China sub-2% property-hit but India PLI 12% electronics, TSMC/Micron SEA upside. Rest of world (5%) 5% on Australia, LatAm mining.

Our SmartForge IoT on machining centers, shipped 2,500 units year-to-date at 85% attach, boosts throughput 15-20%.

Medium-term 2026-2028: 7-9% CAGR outpacing GDP on Industry 4.0 to $250 billion annual automation capex per McKinsey. Drivers: $1 trillion US onshoring by 2030 positioning our cobots like Fanuc/ABB; 15% CAGR electrification for EV welders, hydrogen compressors amid EU CBAM, SEC rules; AI edge computing for 25% OEE gains in lights-out factories.

We're investing $450 million fiscal 2025 capex (12% sales), including $150 million German laser-cutting acquisition for precision tools. Partnerships with Rockwell for MES, Siemens digital thread; 70% North American sourcing by 2026 from 40% China. Risks: 8% alloy inflation, geopolitics, PMI below 45 recession. But 92% backlog gross margins insulate us.

Near-term stabilization leads to acceleration; fiscal 2025 revenue 7-9%, EPS $8.50-$9.00 for 15% plus ROIC.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from David Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Chen (Barclays):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the demand environment you're seeing in the semiconductor market?

Johnathan Hale:
Good morning, David. Absolutely, the semiconductor space continues to be a standout for us, representing about 25% of our mix. We're seeing robust pull-through from the AI infrastructure buildout, with hyperscalers driving capex for advanced nodes and high-bandwidth memory. Customers like TSMC and our US fab partners are accelerating via CHIPS Act funding, leading to strong orders for our precision CNC machining centers and wafer handling systems. Utilization surveys show steady gains, and our backlog here is up significantly. Near-term, we expect 10-12% growth in 2025, with medium-term tailwinds from reshoring keeping momentum strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel (JPMorgan):
Thanks. What are your expectations for capital expenditures in the coming year?

Michael Rivera:
Hi Lisa. Our fiscal 2025 capex is planned at around $450 million, or about 12% of sales, in line with our prior guide. This includes continued investment in nearshoring like the Monterrey robotics fab, digital upgrades such as expanding SmartForge and Dynalink IoT platforms, and R&D for electrification plays like 48V actuators and hydrogen components. Roughly 40% targets high-return renewables and automation, with the rest maintaining our asset base. This supports our free cash flow outlook while positioning for 7-9% end-market CAGR through 2028. We're disciplined, focusing on projects with ROIC above 15%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. How are you managing supply chain disruptions, and what impact are they having on your margins?

Johnathan Hale:
Morning, Robert. Supply chain remains a focus, but we've made great strides through multi-sourcing and localization—now at 70% North American by 2026 target, down from heavy China reliance. Red Sea issues bumped steel 6%, but pricing discipline and lean sigma efficiencies offset that, contributing to our 210 basis point consolidated margin expansion. In segments like aerospace, we normalized titanium flows for 150 basis points gain; energy renewables via India localization cut logistics 18%. Aftermarket IoT predictive tools further de-risk by slashing downtimes 22%. Overall, minimal margin drag this quarter, and we're insulated via backlog pricing.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Industrio Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
